definition: Compress means to press or squeeze something together so that it takes up less space.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word compress. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know compress should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The machine at the recycling plant can compress hundreds of aluminum cans into a single dense cube.
You can squeeze a sponge gently with one hand; to compress it is to force it fully into a smaller space.
Compressing something packs it tighter but leaves it whole; crushing it destroys its shape completely.

To compact something is to pack it down tightly so it holds together — machines compact trash, snow compacts underfoot. Compress is broader: it covers any pressing into less space, gentle or forceful, and extends to shrinking digital files. Compacting packs material solid; compressing simply forces it smaller.

To condense something is to make it denser, shorter, or more concentrated, and it is the usual word for shrinking words and ideas — you condense a chapter into a summary. Compress is the physical counterpart: you compress air, springs, and luggage by squeezing them into less space.

To cram is to stuff things forcibly into a space that barely holds them — cramming clothes into a suitcase. Compress reduces the thing itself, forcing it to take up less room; cram just jams items into a tight container, leaving each item the same size as before.

Rolling slowly along the line, the press would compress each mattress to a tenth of its thickness, squeezing the air out through the foam's open cells.
Sealed in plastic while still flattened, the mattress could ride to a customer in a box the size of a mini-fridge.
